title: How to Spot Fake Discount Codes for Days Out
description: Why so many days out discount codes don’t work, how to spot fake or expired codes and copycat ticket sites, and where to find genuine offers instead.
h1: How to spot fake discount codes for days out
intro: You search for “theme park discount code”, find a page of codes, and none of them work. Here’s why that happens, and how to find the real savings instead.

image.alt: A family flying a kite in a field under a clear blue sky

cardText: Why codes fail, how to spot copycat ticket sites and where real deals live.

blocks.title: Scout’s sniff test
blocks.text: If a code claims a huge discount on an attraction that never discounts, it’s almost certainly fake. Check the attraction’s own offers page first.
points: Real offers usually appear on the official site
Look for a date checked or expiry date
Never pay by bank transfer to a stranger for tickets

sections.h2: Why so many codes don’t work
sections.html: Some voucher sites list every code they’ve ever seen to rank in search results, including codes that expired long ago, were for one customer only, or never existed. That’s why HappyDaysOut only lists offers we’ve checked, with the date.

• No expiry date or “last checked” date.
  • “Reveal code” buttons that open lots of pop-ups.
  • Huge discounts on attractions that rarely discount, like popular studio tours.
  • Ticket sites with prices far below the official price, or that ask for payment by bank transfer.

Search ads sometimes lead to unofficial sellers. Check the web address carefully, buy from the attraction or an authorised seller, and pay by card for extra protection. Unofficial tickets can be refused at the gate.

• Kids-go-free rules and family tickets.
  • 2FOR1 with train tickets.
  • Annual passes and memberships.
  • Off-peak, date-based pricing.

faqs.a: Many listed codes have expired, were single-use, or never existed. Genuine offers usually appear on the attraction’s official website or come from official schemes.

faqs.q: How do I know if a ticket website is official?
faqs.a: Check the web address matches the attraction’s official site, look for it being listed as an authorised seller, and be wary of prices far below official ones.
